scope: Three targeted native diagnostic runs on one local SID. No music bytes, ROM or PCM payload is included. Production sources and published WASM were not modified.

initialStop.operation: BNE in a normal indirect-indexed memory-copy loop, not a CPU JAM or ROM access

copy.explanation: The 32-page copy alone exceeds 100k cycles. The source and destination pointers advance normally; no iteration limit was bypassed.

changes: Copied the production core header into /private/tmp and made third-party includes absolute.
Made private diagnostic state readable in the scratch header only.
Replaced initBudget with SID_DIAG_INIT_BUDGET; compiled one 100k baseline and two 2M diagnostics.
Expanded only the scratch retained-audio queue from 16384 to 131072 frames (524288 bytes at Float32).
CPU/SID source, clock, bank behavior, I/O policy and play 16k limit were unchanged.

nextFailure.interpretation: A real CIA1 Timer A low-byte write. Nearby code also conditionally writes the high byte at $DC05; this is not an indexed-store dummy read.

conclusions: The 100k init timeout is reproducible and caused by legitimate longer initialization, which returns at 132113 cycles in the scratch host.
Increasing the init limit alone is insufficient: the first play routine then requires actual CIA I/O.
Future work needs a longer bounded initialization policy with retained-PCM capacity checks AND full-machine VBI execution, preserving original VBI timing and header bytes.
Do not silently switch the file to CIA-speed, bypass real I/O, or claim playback success from the init return alone.
